  "text": "At eight on Tuesday morning, the envelope was still under Mara’s door. She had noticed its corner when she came downstairs, but she stepped over it on her way to the kitchen. The post usually came after nine. For a moment she wondered whether it had been there since yesterday.

The kettle took longer than usual to boil. Mara opened the cupboard, took out a mug and found that she was holding two. She put one back. On the calendar beside the fridge, her mother’s appointment was written in blue ink, with the time underlined. Mara had crossed out the previous week’s errands as she finished them, but she had left the appointment alone. It hadn’t been hers to finish.

She poured water over a teabag and carried the mug to the table. From there she could see the envelope in the hall. It was plain white, with no address showing, and too far away for her to tell whether anyone had written on it at all. She could also see the answering machine on the shelf beneath the mirror. Its light blinked steadily.

Mara drank her tea while it was too hot. She had a train to catch in forty minutes, and there were clean clothes upstairs she had not yet put away. Neither seemed urgent. She set the mug down and tried to remember exactly when she had last spoken to her mother. Sunday, she thought, though they had only talked about the weather and a loose cupboard handle.

Yesterday had gone differently from the way she’d planned."
